# Python Data Structures, Concurrency, Testing, Profiling, Database Transactions, and API Design

This comprehensive guide covers six critical areas of Python software engineering. Each section includes concrete, runnable examples with explanations.

## 1. Python Data Structures

### 1.1 Built-in Collections

```python
from collections import defaultdict, deque, Counter, namedtuple, OrderedDict
from typing import Any, List, Dict, Set, Tuple

# --- List: Ordered, mutable, O(1) append, O(n) insert/delete ---
numbers: List[int] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
numbers.append(6)          # O(1) amortized
numbers.insert(0, 0)       # O(n) - shifts all elements
del numbers[2]             # O(n)
numbers.pop()              # O(1) - removes last element
numbers.sort()             # O(n log n) - in-place
numbers.reverse()          # O(n)

# --- Tuple: Immutable, hashable, O(1) access ---
point: Tuple[int, int] = (3, 4)
# point[0] = 10  # TypeError: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment
point_hash = hash(point)  # Tuples are hashable (if all elements are)

# --- Set: Unordered, unique, O(1) average lookup/insert/delete ---
unique_numbers: set = {1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 4}
print(len(unique_numbers))  # 4
if 3 in unique_numbers:    # O(1) average
    print("3 is in the set")
union = {1, 2} | {3, 4}    # {1, 2, 3, 4}
intersection = {1, 2, 3} & {2, 3, 4}  # {2, 3}
symmetric_difference = {1, 2} ^ {2, 3}  # {1, 3}

# --- Dict: Ordered (3.7+), O(1) average lookup/insert/delete ---
user: Dict[str, Any] = {"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "scores": [90, 85, 95]}
user["email"] = "alice@example.com"
if "name" in user:
    print(user["name"])
user.pop("age", None)  # Safe pop with default
user.setdefault("role", "user")  # Sets only if key doesn't exist

# --- defaultdict: Dict with a default factory ---
word_count: Dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
for word in "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog the end".split():
    word_count[word] += 1
print(word_count["the"])  # 3
print(word_count["zebra"])  # 0 (auto-created)

# --- deque: Double-ended queue, O(1) append/pop on both ends ---
queue: deque = deque([1, 2, 3])
queue.append(4)       # O(1)
queue.appendleft(0)   # O(1)
queue.popleft()       # O(1) - removes from left
queue.pop()           # O(1) - removes from right
# Use deque for queues, stacks, sliding windows, BFS
from collections import deque as dq
bfs_queue = dq([1])
bfs_queue.append(2)
bfs_queue.append(3)

# --- Counter: Dict subclass for counting ---
scores = [90, 85, 90, 95, 85, 90]
score_counts = Counter(scores)
print(score_counts)  # Counter({90: 3, 85: 2, 95: 1})
print(score_counts.most_common(2))  # [(90, 3), (85, 2)]
score_counts.update([90, 90])
print(score_counts[90])  # 5

# --- namedtuple: Lightweight immutable object ---
Point = namedtuple("Point", ["x", "y"])
p = Point(3, 4)
print(p.x, p.y)  # 3 4
p = p._replace(x=10)  # p = Point(x=10, y=4)
# p.x = 5  # AttributeError: 'Point' object has no attribute 'x' (immutable)
